recipes.name: Easy Potato Salad with Dill
ingredients_raw: 1 pound red potatoes, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
2 sprigs chopped fresh dill, or to taste
0.5 cucumber - peeled, seeded, and finely chopped

steps.text: Place potatoes in a large pot; cover with salted water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until tender, about 12 minutes. Drain; steam dry while preparing dressing.
Whisk mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, dill, salt, and black pepper together in a large bowl; stir in green onions and cucumber.
Add warm potatoes to dressing; toss gently to coat. Cover bowl; refrigerate before serving, at least 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Potato Salad with Dill
raw_recipe.description: This easy potato salad with dill recipe calls for red potatoes tossed with a creamy mayo-based cucumber and dill dressing. Cucumbers add some crunch.

review.reviewBody: I had only russet potatoes, so that's what I used, and I had no fresh dill, so used dried. For our taste, 2 Tbsp cider vinegar was too much because it really thinned out the dressing (it was almost like a salad dressing) and was a little too tart for us...I added a pinch of sugar. I compensated on the dressing consistency by adding more mayo which yielded a nice smooth dressing that wasn't falling off of the potatoes. This was a nice change from the typical mayo-based potato salad, and in the future, I will reduce the vinegar to 1 Tbsp. Thanks, bonmot, for sharing your recipe. UPDATE 8.17.12 I had some left from dinner and was surprised this morning when I looked in the fridge that it held up great! Wondered if the cukes would break down overnight, making it runny. It looks exactly like it did yesterday. Sooooo you can make it ahead of time with no concern that it'll be runny the next day.

We had this tonight because it had no celery and it was very tasty! I had to make a couple of substitutions based on what I had: rice vinegar for the cider vinegar and bell pepper for the cucumber. We will definitely have this again because it is super easy and we normally have some type of crunchy vegetable on hand. It paired very well with roasted red pepper grilled chicken and grilled corn - the mild vinegar really complemented the rest of the meal. We will definitely have again. Update: I have made this more times than I can count. Sometimes I use dill pickle juice instead of vinegar and add whatever crunchy vegetables I have. This is by far my family's favorite mayo based potato salad. You can't go wrong with it.

This was a simple potato salad that turned out great. I used baby reds (less chopping), only used 3 green onions (preference) and added more dill (I love dill!). My guests and my husband really liked it. I also liked it because my husband and I don't like white onions or celery, so the cucumbers and green onions were a good fit for us. I thought it was easy to make and everyone enjoyed it. I was worried that there was not enough dressing at first, however it was fine after mixing it all up. Good for people who don't like a heavy dressing or a heavy mayo tasting salad. This will probably be my go to potato salad from now on.

This is a tasty potato salad. I used the reds because I had them on hand, substituted 1/4 cup for miracle whip for mayo, because that's what I use and I added 1/4 cup sour cream, used 1T apple cider vinegar and 1T pickle juice (clausen kosher dill), added 1/4 cup cooked bacon, fresh parsley, chives & dill because that's what I have growing in my garden, s&p to taste and paprika. I should add that I rarely follow recipes, but rather use them as a base of inspiration to create my own. Next time, I'll try to follow the recipe explicitly.

Only three green onion stalks, four was overpowering. Only one tablespoon of apple cider vinegar. THIS. IS. AMAZING. THOUGH! One more recommendation: double the recipe because you’re going to want more. My teen and I almost demolished The whole thing before it even cooled off. Six stars!

I was short on time but needed something to go with a Rotisserie chicken A few simple ingredients and I wasn’t chopping all day. I only had russets and used 2 large - peeled and chopped perhaps bigger than suggested but I have a bad habit of overcooking! I only cooked 8 minutes (hate mushy potatoes). Following other viewers, I reduced vinegar to 1 tbsp and added an extra tbsp of mayo plus a pinch if sugar. My husband requested to add celery next time which would be easy to do. Thanks!

Needed a quick side to make with a can of diced potatoes. Made this recipe subbing with 1/2 lite and 1/2 low fat mayo, chives and a cucumber from the garden, dried dill, let sit for about 20 minutes and was DELICIOUS!

Absolutely loved this potato salad. I used an English cucumber (sliced and cut it halves), dried dill, and four cooked bacon slices chopped. We served it with teriyaki chicken kabobs, with green and red peppers, onions, and mushrooms. I would give this salad 10 stars!!!

I didn't have green onions so I used a red one the first time I made it and today, I used a yellow onion (so to answer if I would make it again there you have it) . this was so easy to make, I did add about 2 tablespoons of miracle whip as that is what I put in my Mac Salad!!

Delicious.
Big hit! I used a little less of the apple cider vinegar based on the other comments. I used extra baby cucumbers, too, because I had them. Everyone really liked it!

I thought this tasted good. I liked how fairly quick it was to make and that it had a crunch, but not from raw celery and onions. I did only get about 3 servings though. After I started making it I realized I only had 1 green onion, so I just used that. For the dill I subbed 2 small pinches of dry as it is more affordable and what I had on hand. I also cooled the potatoes, ran them under some cold water, and then refridgerated them after draining for about 1 hour. For the dressing I used white wine vinegar with lite mayo. However, I think I would prefer the cider vinegar and regular mayo. My dressing got a little thin, which I believe was from using lite mayo. That was my fault though. Ty

I changed this a little - we like mustard in our potato salad so added a touch of that along with onion powder (no one likes to bite into an onion in the salad). I always dilute my lite mayo with dill pickle juice!! Plus I add some dill pickle relish and of course hard boiled eggs...old family recipe and it always disappears in no time at all!!
Yummy! I made my own mayonnaise in a blender (took an extra 5 minutes) and it turned out great!
Really tasty. Fresh alternative for standard potato salad that's great in the summer.

Yes, I made changes. Like others said, 2 teaspoons of the vinegar was too much. I added more mayo, some regular white onions, some Splenda, because the vinegar was just too much. I also added some sour cream. Probably won't make it again.
I used yellow and red peppers instead of cucumbers because that is what I had.
It ranks as one of my favorite potato salad recipes
SO amazing!! this makes me want new potatoes and fresh dill ALL YEAR ROUND!
Love this simple but tasty side dish!
